If sentiment is positive (≥0.5) in the last 3 days, adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture bullish momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to reflect bearish pressure.

If sentiment is neutral (0.0–0.49) and forecast is trending upward, apply a 1–2% downward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent over-optimism.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, apply a 1–2% upward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to avoid premature pessimism.

In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment shifts from negative to positive, apply a 1–3% upward correction to capture reversal momentum.

If sentiment remains consistently negative across 5+ days, apply a 2–4% downward correction across all horizons to reflect entrenched bearish sentiment.
